Some teams agree not to use parts of the `jest` object, like module mocks, fake timers or spies. This rule reports the methods you list, with your own message if you give one, so the agreement doesn't depend on review.

The rule does nothing until you give it a list.

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun:test/no-restricted-jest-methods" = "error" # or "warn"
```

## Examples

These examples restrict `advanceTimersByTime` and `spyOn`.

Reported:

```ts
import { expect, jest, test } from "bun:test";

test("retries after a second", () => {
  const send = jest.spyOn(mailer, "send");
  retry(send);
  jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
  expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
});
```

Not reported:

```ts
import { expect, jest, test } from "bun:test";

test("retries once", () => {
  const send = jest.fn();
  retry(send);
  expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
});
```

`vi` is checked the same way as `jest`:

```ts
import { vi } from "bun:test";

const send = vi.spyOn(mailer, "send");
```

Only methods of `jest` and `vi` are checked. The `spyOn` and `mock` functions that `"bun:test"` exports aren't:

```ts
import { spyOn } from "bun:test";

const send = spyOn(mailer, "send");
```

## Options

The rule takes one object. Each key is a method name, and its value is the message to report.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun:test/no-restricted-jest-methods" = ["error", {
  spyOn = "Pass the dependency in instead of spying on it",
}]
```

In a JSON or JavaScript config, use `null` in place of the message to get the default message: ``Use of `spyOn` is not allowed``.
